prompt:
Scene:
A square-format 90s flash close-up photograph of a rectangular pool return vent set into the side wall of a drained basin, shot from within the basin itself at shoulder height. Direct flash fully illuminates the vent; the surrounding tile glows from the reflected light. Background recedes into darker basin shadow. Fine 35mm film grain, slight warm yellow cast.

Subject:
A stainless-steel return vent approximately 15 centimeters wide, with horizontal slats, mounted into the aqua-tiled wall of the pool. Mineral deposits have left faint white streaks on the tile directly below the vent. Around the vent, tile grout is discolored chlorine-yellow. The basin floor is visible at the bottom edge of frame: dry concrete, small drain grate.

Important details:
Close-up realism is essential: steel slats must show minor scratches, tile grout must be specific, mineral streak must feel decade-old. The flash hotspot should concentrate on the vent center with clear falloff toward corners. The image must feel like a maintenance-inspection snapshot, not art photography. No water flowing. No reflection of photographer on steel.

Use case:
Empty Pool single study 5/5, tight material study of a return vent inside a drained basin.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no water, no reflection of photographer, no dramatic framing, no cinematic grade.
